main_text.p: mo dicunt, & Latini ad marginē a Latroci-nali[?] pro Photio,&Tertiam pro illius restitu-tione a fua, quæ pro Ignatio fuit, distinguunt.

Historias turpiter confundunt, dum aduersarios aiunt calumniari Ioannem Octavum, ut fœminæ, quam viro similhorem[?], quod tanta lenitate in redarguendis Photii impostoris usus esset. Ioannis lenitatem in expetendis scelerum poenis a Photio non modo Latini, sed Græci etiam ipsi criminati sunt, non damnan-tes Concilium vocatum Oecumenicū octavum a Latinis, quasi Apostolicos Canones violasset, sed ex rebus, quæ post Concilium evenerunt, maiorem severitatem desiderantes: quippe videbatur clementius egisse, quam per Canones ipsos agere licuisset, si summo iure agere cum Photio, Photianisque voluisset: Nicetas de vita sancti Ignatij; αὐτὸν τι ἡ Φώτιον διὰ ταῦτα καθαιρεῖν ἰδή[?], καὶ ὃν θεῷ καὶ θηρηνιῷ[?] ὀρτονεῖδις καὶ πίζις[?], καὶ σὺν κακοιωνικὸς ἡ αὐτὸ[?] ἀποφάσει πάντας, καὶ μὴ φιλανθρωπότερος Θεῷ[?], καὶ Θεῷ γινωσκόντες κείσεως τὴν ἀνάφασιν τὲ πανα-γίᾳ[?] πιθανῷ ἀνέχεσθαι. τοῦτο τὰ ἀγὼν κάπω[?] πα-ποίηκε. τέτο δ' κείμεσθε[?] ἐκ ἐστὶν ὅσον ἀπᾶν κακῶν ἄνδρ[?] καὶ σκανδάλων ἐχεμάπρου[?]. Οἶμαι γὰρ ὡς εἰ Ἀποστολικῶς τότε καὶ καθονικῶς τῇ πάντων ἀπο-φώσαντος, ὃ τὸν ἀπὸ μόνον τῆς ἀληθείας τε, καὶ τῷ σκανδάλῳ, ἀλλὰ καὶ σὺν κοινωνίζαντας ἀυτῆ[?]

page.notes: Printed page 45, single column of text with Latin and Greek. The Greek passage (Nicetas, Vita S. Ignatii) is only partly legible at this scan resolution: words marked [?] are best readings, and the Greek accents may be inexact. The "nal‡" at the start of line 1 shows a small mark after "nal" that I read as "nali[?]". Red and orange stains and small bullet dots on the page are not printed text and are not transcribed. No running head is printed. The catchword at the lower right is the Greek word "ἀυτῆ", as printed.
